approved: Universities Accord (Australian Tertiary Education Commission) (Consequential and Transitional Provisions) Bill 2025
Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
This bill is part of a package that establishes the Australian Tertiary Education Commission (ATEC) as the steward of the higher education system.
The package would create a National Tertiary Education Objective, require ATEC to consider it, and set up a three-member commission with a First Nations Commissioner.
The package would also introduce mission-based compacts with higher education providers, which could lead to compliance action if not in force for a year.
Establishes the Australian Tertiary Education Commission (ATEC) as the steward of the higher education system.
Creates a National Tertiary Education Objective (NTEO) that ATEC must have regard to.
Provides for ATEC to be led by three independent commissioners, including a First Nations Commissioner.
Requires ATEC to establish a First Nations Advisory Committee.
Introduces mission-based compacts with higher education providers, with potential compliance action under HESA if not in force.
Embeds equity by requiring ATEC to consider improving outcomes for people facing systemic barriers to education.
Higher education providers, students, First Nations communities, and people facing systemic barriers to education.

The majority voted in favour of a [motion](https://www.openaustralia.org.au/debates/?id=2026-02-10.6.1) to agree with the main idea of the bill. In parliamentary jargon, they voted to read the bill for a second time. ### What does this bill do? According to the [bills digest](https://www.aph.gov.au/Parliamentary_Business/Bills_Legislation/bd/bd2526/26bd038), which is a document prepared by the parliamentary library: > *The Universities Accord (Australian Tertiary Education Commission) (Consequential and Transitional Provisions) Bill 2025 (the C&T Bill) amends related legislation to implement the Bill, including transferring responsibilities for the Higher Education Standards Framework to [Australian Tertiary Education Commission (ATEC)](https://www.aph.gov.au/Parliamentary_Business/Bills_Legislation/bd/bd2526/26bd038), and enabling information sharing between the Department of Education and ATEC.*

Argued that the Universities Accord (Australian Tertiary Education Commission) Bill 2025 and related bill would create another regulator without a clear educational vision, embed inappropriate objectives concerning social development and environmental sustainability, and add to duplication, cost and regulatory complexity, while acknowledging equity and workforce considerations.

Moved to suspend standing and sessional orders, but the Deputy Speaker ruled the proposed motion irrelevant to the bill before the House; then supported bills establishing the Australian Tertiary Education Commission under the Universities Accord, describing its proposed stewardship, equity, funding and provider oversight functions before the debate was interrupted under standing order 43.

Moved procedural motions to expedite consideration of legislation and limit debate, then criticised the government for scheduling 22 bills for rapid passage and alleged that the process lacked transparency and scrutiny.

Criticised the Universities Accord bills as rushed, over-regulatory and insufficiently independent, while other contributions argued that the Australian Tertiary Education Commission would provide long-term stewardship, coordinate higher and vocational education, and improve access and outcomes; the bills later passed with amendments.
